subject: maths
title: Year 5 Metric Units: Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Year 5 Metric Units Worksheets: Length, Mass and Capacity (Free Maths with Answer Key)
standard_text: Choose appropriate metric units when measuring the length, mass and capacity of objects; use smaller units or a combination of units to obtain a more accurate measure
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on metric units, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5M01): choose mm, cm, m, km, g, kg, t, mL or L, read rulers, scales and jugs accurately, combine units like 1 m 35 cm, convert units and solve word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Choose a unit that fits the size, and use smaller units for a more accurate measure.
key_sub: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 L = 1000 mL. So 1 m 35 cm = 135 cm and 2 kg 40 g = 2040 g, not 240 g.
body_html:
Choose a unit that fits

Small things use small units. Big things use big units. Think of something you know of about that size.

MeasureUnits (small to big)About the size of
Lengthmm, cm, m, km1 mm: the thickness of a 5c coin. 1 cm: the width of a fingertip. 1 m: a big step. 1 km: about 10 minutes’ walk
Massg, kg, t1 g: a paper clip. 1 kg: a bag of sugar. 1 t: a small car
CapacitymL, L5 mL: a teaspoon. 375 mL: a can of soft drink. 1 L: a carton of milk
Facts to know
1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm   1 km = 1000 m
1 kg = 1000 g   1 t = 1000 kg
1 L = 1000 mL

Smaller units give a more accurate measure

“About 7 cm” is not exact. Count the small marks too and use millimetres, or use two units together.

On a scale or a jug, first work out what one mark is worth: the jump between two numbers ÷ the number of spaces.

Combine units

Change the big unit into the small unit, then add the rest.

Metres and centimetres

1 m 35 cm = ☐ cm

1 m = 100 cm. 100 + 35 = 135.

Answer: 135 cm

Kilograms and grams

2 kg 40 g = ☐ g

2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 + 40 = 2040.

Answer: 2040 g (not 240 g)

Litres and millilitres

1650 mL = ☐ L ☐ mL

1000 mL = 1 L. 1650 − 1000 = 650.

Answer: 1 L 650 mL

Convert between units

Big unit to small unit: multiply (you need more of the small units). Small unit to big unit: divide.

Kilograms to grams

3.5 kg = ☐ g

1 kg = 1000 g. 3.5 × 1000 = 3500.

Answer: 3500 g

Millilitres to litres

750 mL = ☐ L

1 L = 1000 mL. 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75.

Answer: 0.75 L

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1 m = 10 cm or 1 m = 1000 cm1 m = 100 cm. It is 1 cm = 10 mm and 1 km = 1000 m
2 kg 40 g = 240 g2 kg = 2000 g, so 2 kg 40 g = 2040 g
Counting every mark on a scale as 1, 10 or 100Work out what one mark is worth first
Forgetting that an object does not start at 0Take the start away from the end
Comparing numbers without units (450 mL > 0.5 L)Change to the same unit: 0.5 L = 500 mL
Choosing a unit from the wrong measure (kg for a bottle of water’s capacity)Length: mm, cm, m, km. Mass: g, kg, t. Capacity: mL, L

faq.q: What metric units do Year 5 students use in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 5 students choose and use millimetres, centimetres, metres and kilometres for length, grams, kilograms and tonnes for mass, and millilitres and litres for capacity.

faq.q: Why do Year 5 students use smaller units or a combination of units?
faq.a: Smaller units give a more accurate measure. A pencil that is “about 16 cm” can be measured more accurately as 164 mm or 16 cm 4 mm.

faq.q: How do you change 2 kg 40 g into grams?
faq.a: Change the kilograms into grams first: 2 kg = 2000 g. Then add the grams: 2000 + 40 = 2040 g, not 240 g.

faq.q: Is measurement part of the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: Yes. NAPLAN numeracy includes measurement, so Year 5 students may be asked to choose units, read scales and convert between units such as metres and centimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of an ant?
items.e: Most ants are shorter than 1 cm, so use millimetres. A centimetre is too big to show its length well.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a netball court?
items.e: A netball court is about 30 m long. You can walk along it in under a minute, so use metres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the distance from Sydney to Canberra?
items.e: Sydney to Canberra is a long drive of a few hours, so use kilometres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a watermelon?
items.e: A watermelon is heavy to carry but much lighter than a car, so use kilograms. Tonnes are for very heavy things like trucks.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a 20c coin?
items.e: A coin is very light, so use grams. A 20c coin has a mass of about 11 g.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a loaded truck?
items.e: A loaded truck is very heavy, so use tonnes. 1 t = 1000 kg.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much medicine fits on a teaspoon?
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 mL, so use millilitres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so use litres. Kilograms measure mass, not capacity.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the height of a tall gum tree?
items.e: A tall gum tree is many metres high. Centimetres would give a huge number, and kilometres are far too big.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the thickness of a $1 coin?
items.e: A coin is only a few millimetres thick. That is much less than 1 cm, so use millimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a pencil case?
items.e: A pencil case fits on a 30 cm ruler, so use centimetres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a kangaroo?
items.e: A grown kangaroo is about as heavy as an adult person, so use kilograms.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much a can of soft drink holds?
items.e: A can holds less than 1 litre (375 mL), so use millilitres. Grams and kilograms measure mass.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a marathon race?
items.e: A marathon is about 42 km. It takes runners hours, so use kilometres.

items.q: Choose the best estimate for the mass of a family car.
items.e: A family car is about 1500 kg, which is 1.5 t. 1500 g is only as heavy as one and a half bags of sugar.

items.q: Choose the best estimate for the capacity of a school water bottle.
items.e: Most drink bottles hold 500 mL to 1 L, so 750 mL fits. 75 L would fill a big rubbish bin.

items.q: Choose the best estimate for the height of a Year 5 student.
items.e: Most Year 5 students are between 1 m 30 cm and 1 m 50 cm tall, so 140 cm fits. 140 mm is only 14 cm, the size of a hand.

items.q: Jack measures his book. It is between 24 cm and 25 cm long. Which unit should he use to give a more accurate measure?
items.e: A smaller unit gives a more accurate measure. 1 cm = 10 mm, so he can measure to the nearest millimetre, for example 247 mm.

items.q: Mia’s bag of apples is between 1 kg and 2 kg. Which is the most accurate way to record its mass?
items.e: Using kilograms and grams together gives a more accurate measure than whole kilograms. 1 kg 350 g tells exactly where the mass is between 1 kg and 2 kg.

items.q: Which measure of a pencil is the most accurate?
items.e: Millimetres are the smallest unit here. 164 mm (16 cm 4 mm) is more accurate than 16 cm, which leaves out the extra 4 mm.

sets.title: Read rulers, scales and jugs accurately

items.e: The pencil starts at 0. It ends 4 small marks past 7 cm. 7 cm = 70 mm, and 70 + 4 = 74 mm. (80 mm reads the next number, 8, instead of counting the small marks.)
The crayon starts at 2 cm, not 0. It ends at 8 cm 3 mm. 83 mm − 20 mm = 63 mm = 6 cm 3 mm. (8 cm 3 mm forgets that the crayon does not start at 0.)
The eraser starts at 1 cm (10 mm) and ends at 48 mm. 48 − 10 = 38 mm. (48 mm forgets that it starts at 1 cm. 30 mm counts only the whole centimetres.)
The ribbon ends 5 small marks past 10 cm. 10 cm = 100 mm, and 100 + 5 = 105 mm. (150 mm reads 10 cm 5 mm as 1 and 50.)
The pencil ends 7 small marks past 9 cm, so it is 9 cm 7 mm (97 mm). 9 cm and 10 cm are only to the nearest centimetre. 97 cm uses the wrong unit.
The crayon ends 8 small marks past 5 cm, so it is 5 cm 8 mm (58 mm). 6 cm is the nearest whole centimetre, but 5 cm 8 mm is more accurate.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg and 4 × 100 = 400 g, so 1 kg 400 g. (1 kg 40 g counts each mark as 10 g.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg and 3 × 250 = 750 g, so 2 kg 750 g. (2 kg 300 g counts each mark as 100 g.)
Each kilogram is split into 5 spaces, so each mark is 1000 ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 3 marks past 3 kg: 3 kg and 3 × 200 = 600 g, so 3 kg 600 g. (3 kg 300 g counts each mark as 100 g.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bunch of bananas. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g and there are 4 spaces between them, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 50 = 650 g. (610 g counts each mark as 10 g, and 700 g counts each mark as 100 g.)

The numbers go up by 100 g and there are 5 spaces between them, so each mark is 100 ÷ 5 = 20 g. The needle is 3 marks past 300: 300 + 60 = 360 g. (330 g counts each mark as 10 g. 400 g reads the next number.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g and there are 5 spaces between them, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 1500: 1500 + 300 = 1800 g. (1530 g counts each mark as 10 g.)
Each mark is 100 g, so the needle is at 1 kg 300 g = 1300 g. 2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 − 1300 = 700 g more.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in L and mL.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL and there are 2 spaces between them, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line above 1000: 1000 + 250 = 1250 mL. (1 L 100 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL and there are 4 spaces between them, so each line is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 600: 600 + 150 = 750 mL. (630 mL counts each line as 10 mL, and 900 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in L and mL.
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 2 lines above 2 L: 2 L and 2 × 250 = 500 mL, so 2 L 500 mL. (2 L 200 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1 L: 1 L and 3 × 250 = 750 mL, so 1 L 750 mL. (1300 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL and there are 5 spaces between them, so each line is 100 ÷ 5 = 20 mL. The water is 2 lines above 400: 400 + 40 = 440 mL. (420 mL counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL and there are 5 spaces between them, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 2 lines above 750: 750 + 100 = 850 mL. (770 mL counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 L?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL, so the water is at 1400 mL. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 − 1400 = 600 mL more. (1400 mL is the water already in the jug.)

sets.title: Combine units: m and cm, kg and g, L and mL

items.q: 1 m 35 cm = ☐ cm

items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 + 40 = 2040 g. The 40 g is 4 tens, so the hundreds digit is 0. (240 g just joins 2 and 40. 2400 g puts the 4 in the hundreds place.)

items.q: 3 m 5 cm = ☐ cm
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. 300 + 5 = 305 cm. (35 cm just joins 3 and 5. 350 cm would be 3 m 50 cm.)

items.q: 4 cm 7 mm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 4 cm = 40 mm. 40 + 7 = 47 mm. (407 mm uses 1 cm = 100 mm. 11 mm adds 4 + 7.)

items.q: 3 L 75 mL = ☐ mL
58 mm = ☐ cm ☐ mm
items.e: 10 mm = 1 cm, so 50 mm = 5 cm. 58 − 50 = 8, so 58 mm = 5 cm 8 mm.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1 m 80 cm = 180 cm and 1 m 8 cm = 108 cm. 180 cm is more than 170 cm and 118 cm, so 1 m 80 cm is the longest.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 2 kg 50 g = 2050 g, 2 kg 5 g = 2005 g and 2 kg 400 g = 2400 g. 2500 g is the heaviest.

items.q: Which is the same as 1 L 500 mL?

items.e: 60 cm + 70 cm = 130 cm. 130 cm = 1 m 30 cm, so trade 100 cm for 1 m: 1 m + 1 m 30 cm = 2 m 30 cm. (1 m 30 cm forgets to add the traded metre. 2 m 3 cm reads 130 cm as 1 m 3 cm.)
You cannot take 500 mL from 200 mL, so trade 1 L for 1000 mL: 3 L 200 mL = 2 L 1200 mL. 1200 − 500 = 700 mL and 2 − 1 = 1 L, so 1 L 700 mL. (2 L 300 mL takes 200 from 500 instead.)
1 m = 100 cm. A metre ruler has 100 centimetres on it. (10 is the number of mm in 1 cm, and 1000 is the number of mm in 1 m.)
Kilo means 1000, so 1 km = 1000 m.
1 tonne = 1000 kg. A small car is about 1 t.
1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 6 × 100 = 600. So 6 m = 600 cm. (60 cm uses 1 m = 10 cm.)
1 kg = 1000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1000: 4000 ÷ 1000 = 4. So 4000 g = 4 kg.
1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 3.5 × 1000 = 3500. So 3.5 kg = 3500 g. (350 g multiplies by 100, not 1000.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1000: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75. So 750 mL = 0.75 L. Check: 0.75 L is three quarters of a litre.
1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 2.5 × 100 = 250. So 2.5 m = 250 cm.
1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 1.2 × 1000 = 1200. So 1.2 km = 1200 m. (120 m multiplies by 100, not 1000.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.5 × 1000 = 500. So 0.5 L = 500 mL. Half a litre is 500 mL.
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 4.5 × 10 = 45. So 4.5 cm = 45 mm.
1 kg = 1000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1000: 250 ÷ 1000 = 0.25. So 250 g = 0.25 kg. Check: 0.25 kg is a quarter of a kilogram.
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 1.75 × 1000 = 1750. So 1.75 L = 1750 mL.
1 t = 1000 kg. Tonnes are bigger than kilograms, so multiply by 1000: 2.5 × 1000 = 2500. So 2.5 t = 2500 kg.
1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 60 ÷ 100 = 0.6. So 60 cm = 0.6 m. (6 m divides by 10, not 100.)
1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.4 × 100 = 140. So 1.4 m = 140 cm.
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.25 × 1000 = 250. So 0.25 L = 250 mL.

items.q: Which is the same as 1.5 kg?
items.e: 0.5 kg is half a kilogram, which is 500 g. So 1.5 kg = 1 kg 500 g = 1500 g. (1 kg 5 g would be 1.005 kg.)

items.q: Which is the same as 2.3 m?
Which list goes from the smallest to the largest capacity?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 0.4 L = 400 mL and 0.5 L = 500 mL. 400 < 450 < 500. 450 is the biggest number, but 450 mL is less than half a litre.

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, sport and water bottles

items.q: A pancake recipe for 4 people uses 300 mL of milk. Matilda makes pancakes for 8 people. How much milk does she need?
items.e: 8 people is double 4 people, so double the milk: 2 × 300 = 600 mL. (2400 mL multiplies by 8. 150 mL halves instead of doubling.)

items.q: A recipe for Anzac biscuits uses 150 g of flour. Chloe makes 3 batches. How much flour does she use?
items.e: 3 batches: 3 × 150 = 450 g. (153 g adds 3 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: A recipe needs 1.5 kg of potatoes. Mia has 900 g. How many more grams does she need?
items.e: 1.5 kg = 1500 g. 1500 − 900 = 600 g more. (150 g treats 1.5 kg as 1050 g. 2400 g adds instead of finding the difference.)

items.q: To make a jug of cordial, you mix 250 mL of cordial with 1.75 L of water. How much drink does that make?
items.e: Use one unit: 1.75 L = 1750 mL. 250 + 1750 = 2000 mL = 2 L. (251.75 mL adds the numbers without converting.)

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Noah jumps 3 m 45 cm in the long jump. How far is that in centimetres?
In the long jump, Sienna jumps 3 m 20 cm and William jumps 2 m 95 cm. How much further does Sienna jump?
items.e: Use centimetres: 320 − 295 = 25 cm. (1 m 75 cm takes 20 from 95 instead of regrouping 1 m as 100 cm.)

items.q: Four students do the long jump at the athletics carnival. Oliver jumps 2.9 m, Ava jumps 285 cm, Leo jumps 3 m 5 cm and Isla jumps 3.1 m. Who jumps the furthest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 2.9 m = 290 cm, 3 m 5 cm = 305 cm and 3.1 m = 310 cm. 310 cm is the furthest, so Isla wins. 3.1 m is 3 m 10 cm, which is more than 3 m 5 cm.

items.q: In the 4 × 100 m relay, each runner runs 100 m. How far does the whole team run in kilometres?
The school cross-country course is 2.5 km long. Cooper has run 1800 m. How far does he still have to run?
items.e: 2.5 km = 2500 m. 2500 − 1800 = 700 m. (4300 m adds instead. 1300 m takes 5 from 8 instead of regrouping.)

items.q: Zara’s water bottle holds 750 mL. On a hot day she fills it and drinks it all 4 times. How many litres does she drink?
items.e: 4 × 750 = 3000 mL. 1 L = 1000 mL, so 3000 mL = 3 L. (3000 L forgets to change mL into L.)

items.q: A 1.5 L bottle of water is shared equally between 6 cups. How much water goes in each cup?
items.e: 1.5 L = 1500 mL. 1500 ÷ 6 = 250 mL. Check: 6 × 250 = 1500. (0.25 is the answer in litres, not mL.)

items.q: Kai’s 1 L water bottle is full. He drinks 350 mL at recess and 400 mL at lunch. How much water is left?
items.e: 350 + 400 = 750 mL drunk. 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 − 750 = 250 mL left. (750 mL is what was drunk.)

items.q: The school canteen sells water in 600 mL bottles. How many bottles hold 3 L altogether?
Oliver’s school bag has a mass of 4 kg 200 g. He takes out a 650 g lunchbox. What is the mass of the bag now?
items.e: 4 kg 200 g = 4200 g. 4200 − 650 = 3550 g = 3 kg 550 g. (4 kg 450 g takes 200 from 650 instead of regrouping.)

items.q: A truck carries 3 t of sand to a building site. It tips out 1200 kg. How much sand is left on the truck?
items.e: 3 t = 3000 kg. 3000 − 1200 = 1800 kg. (4200 kg adds instead of subtracting. 1800 t has the wrong unit.)

items.q: Charlotte buys 3 bags of mandarins. Each bag has a mass of 750 g. What is the total mass?
Aarav has 2 m of ribbon for a school project. He cuts it into pieces 25 cm long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 ÷ 25 = 8 pieces. (4 pieces is only 1 m. 50 multiplies 2 × 25.)

items.q: Amelia walks 650 m to school and 650 m home every day. How far does she walk in 5 school days, in kilometres?
items.e: There and back is 2 × 650 = 1300 m a day. 5 × 1300 = 6500 m. 6500 ÷ 1000 = 6.5 km. (3.25 km forgets the walk home.)

items.q: A recipe needs 1 kg 200 g of flour. Flour is sold in 500 g bags. How many bags does Leo need to buy?
items.e: 1 kg 200 g = 1200 g. 2 bags = 1000 g, which is not enough. 3 bags = 1500 g, which is enough. (2 bags leaves 200 g short.)

items.q: Which holds more: one 1.25 L bottle or two 600 mL bottles?
c: the two 600 mL bottles, by 50 mL
items.e: 1.25 L = 1250 mL. Two 600 mL bottles hold 2 × 600 = 1200 mL. 1250 − 1200 = 50 mL, so the 1.25 L bottle holds 50 mL more. (650 mL compares it with only one 600 mL bottle.)
